title: Find a Result Worth Teaching
moduleName: Create and Sell Your First Training Programme
learningGoal: Pick a narrow problem and audience with a result they care about, and write a one-sentence learner promise.

items.title: Topic Is Too Large
items.description: Do not sell Everything About Marketing. Instead sell Set Up Your First Referral Follow-Up in One Hour. Narrow focus wins.

items.title: The Formula
items.description: After this programme, [audience] will be able to [specific action or finished item].

items.title: Look for Patterns
items.description: What questions do clients ask repeatedly? What do you explain more than once? What can people practice without you there?

items.title: Audience
items.description: Define precisely enough that they recognize themselves. Not small business owners but consultants who struggle to follow up after speaking events.

items.title: Problem
items.description: Choose one that appears often and can be answered in a short session.

items.title: Result
items.description: Write one result you could demonstrate or check at the end. Something concrete, not feel more successful.

items.title: Speaker
items.description: Create a QR-code follow-up idea after a talk.

items.title: Coach
items.description: Complete a 90-day goal plan.

items.title: Consultant
items.description: Map a single client process.

items.title: Trainer
items.description: Design one productive team meeting.

items.title: Service Provider
items.description: Use a preventive-care checklist.

keyPoint: A first course fails when the topic is too broad. Pick one narrow problem, one specific audience, and one demonstrable result. If you cannot write the learner promise in one sentence, your course is too large.

actionSteps.title: List Three Questions
actionSteps.description: Write down three customer questions you hear often.

actionSteps.title: Choose One Problem
actionSteps.description: Select the question that appears most often and can be answered in a short session.

actionSteps.title: Write the Promise
actionSteps.description: Complete: After this programme, [audience] will be able to [specific result].

nextLessonTitle: Turn the Result into Three Lessons

quizzes.question: Why do most first courses fail at the planning stage?

options.option_text: They are not marketed well enough
The price is too high
They do not have enough video content
The topic is too large and unfocused

quizzes.explanation: Most first courses fail because the topic is too broad. A narrow, specific result attracts committed learners who can actually achieve the promised outcome.

quizzes.question: What should the learner promise look like?

options.option_text: A specific, demonstrable result in one sentence
A guarantee of income or business growth
A broad statement like feel more successful
A list of everything covered in the course

quizzes.explanation: The learner promise should be specific and demonstrable. After this programme, [audience] will be able to [specific action]. Broad claims cannot be checked or measured.

quizzes.question: Where should you look for course ideas?

options.option_text: Questions clients ask repeatedly and work you explain more than once
The most complex service you offer
Competitor websites and market research
Trending topics on social media

quizzes.explanation: The best course ideas come from your existing work. What do clients ask repeatedly? What do you explain more than once? These are proven problems with known demand.

title: Turn the Result into Three Lessons
moduleName: Create and Sell Your First Training Programme
learningGoal: Draft a course structure using the staircase method: understand, practice, finish.

items.title: Lesson 1: Understand
items.description: Explain the problem and give one quick win. The learner sees why this matters and gets an early success.

items.title: Lesson 2: Practice
items.description: Show the method; the learner tries it. This is where the core skill is built.

items.title: Lesson 3: Finish
items.description: Complete the output, review it, and decide what comes next. The learner leaves with something finished.

items.title: Goal
items.description: One sentence stating what the learner will be able to do after this lesson.

items.title: Teaching Point
items.description: One core idea or method explained clearly with a real example.

items.title: Small Action
items.description: One task the learner completes during or immediately after the lesson.

items.title: Done When Test
items.description: A clear description of what successful completion looks like.

items.title: Good Examples
items.description: Draft Your Promise, Map Your Process, Build Your Checklist.

items.title: Avoid
items.description: Introduction to Strategy, Overview of Marketing, Understanding the Basics. These are vague and do not promise a result.

items.title: Mini-Course Length
items.description: Three lessons is enough. No need to invent more sections to look impressive.

keyPoint: The staircase method creates momentum. Lesson 1 gives understanding and a quick win. Lesson 2 builds the core skill through practice. Lesson 3 finishes with a completed output. Each lesson needs a goal, one teaching point, a small action, and a done-when test.

actionSteps.title: Write Three Titles
actionSteps.description: Create action-based titles for each lesson using the staircase method.

actionSteps.title: Describe Learner Activity
actionSteps.description: Write one sentence describing what the learner does in each lesson.

actionSteps.title: Add a Practice Tool
actionSteps.description: Create one worksheet or checklist that helps learners finish the activities.

nextLessonTitle: Build One Useful Lesson Before You Record a Library

quizzes.question: What are the three jobs of Lessons 1, 2, and 3 in the staircase model?

options.option_text: Watch, read, discuss
Introduce, explain, conclude
Understand the problem, practise the method, finish the output
Plan, execute, review

quizzes.explanation: The staircase method uses Lesson 1 for understanding, Lesson 2 for practice, and Lesson 3 for finishing. This creates momentum and ensures learners leave with a completed result.

quizzes.question: How many lessons should a mini-course have?

options.option_text: At least ten to look comprehensive
As many as the topic requires
It depends on the price point
Three lessons is enough

quizzes.explanation: A mini-course can have three lessons. No need to invent more sections to look impressive. Three well-designed lessons that deliver a specific result outperform ten unfocused lessons.

quizzes.question: Which lesson title is better?

options.option_text: Overview of Marketing
Draft Your Promise
Introduction to Strategy
Understanding the Basics

quizzes.explanation: Draft Your Promise is action-based and tells the learner exactly what they will do. Introduction to Strategy is vague and does not promise a result. Action-based titles attract committed learners.

title: Build One Useful Lesson Before You Record a Library
moduleName: Create and Sell Your First Training Programme
learningGoal: Prepare the first lesson and one student tool using a practical four-part sequence.

items.title: Promise (30 seconds)
items.description: Say what the lesson helps them do. This sets expectations and creates motivation.

items.title: Teach (3-5 minutes)
items.description: Explain one idea with a real example. One idea, not five. Real example, not theory.

items.title: Practice (3-5 minutes)
items.description: Give the learner one task. They must do something, not just watch or read.

items.title: Check (30 seconds)
items.description: Describe what successful completion looks like. The learner should know when they have succeeded.

items.title: Video
items.description: Good for demonstrations and personal connection. Does not need professional production — clarity beats polish.

items.title: Text and PDF
items.description: Good for reference material and step-by-step instructions. Always accessible and searchable.

items.title: Slides
items.description: Good for structured explanations. Keep text minimal and visuals clear.

items.title: Combination
items.description: Mix formats based on what serves the learner best. A short video plus a downloadable worksheet often works well.

items.title: Device Accessibility
items.description: Ensure content is readable and accessible on the learner's device. Test on mobile.

items.title: Working Links
items.description: Check all links and file formats. Broken links destroy trust.

items.title: Future Releases
items.description: If parts will be released later, clearly say this before the customer pays and tell them when those parts arrive.

keyPoint: A practical first lesson can be short. Promise, teach, practice, check — four parts, each with a clear job. Do not grade camera quality; grade clarity and the learner's practical result. One usable lesson with a worksheet beats a library of unfinished content.

actionSteps.title: Write the Promise
actionSteps.description: Write what Lesson 1 helps the learner do, in one sentence.

actionSteps.title: Create Teaching Content
actionSteps.description: Write three teaching bullet points with one real example.

actionSteps.title: Design the Exercise
actionSteps.description: Create one task the learner completes and a description of what success looks like.

actionSteps.title: Build the Worksheet
actionSteps.description: Create a worksheet headline and instructions for using it.

quizzes.question: What is the correct order of the four-part lesson sequence?

options.option_text: Teach, practise, promise, check
Promise, teach, practise, check
Check, promise, teach, practise
Practise, teach, check, promise

quizzes.explanation: The correct order is Promise, Teach, Practice, Check. Promise sets expectations, Teach explains the idea, Practice gives a task, and Check defines success.

quizzes.question: What matters more than camera quality?

options.option_text: High-resolution video
Clarity and the learner's practical result
Professional lighting and background
Multiple camera angles

quizzes.explanation: Clarity and the learner's practical result matter more than production quality. A clear phone video that helps someone achieve a result beats a polished studio video that confuses them.

quizzes.question: What should you do if parts of the programme will be released later?

options.option_text: Release all content at once to avoid confusion
Hide this information until after purchase
Promise everything is available immediately
Clearly state this before the customer pays and tell them when parts arrive

quizzes.explanation: If parts will be released later, clearly state this before the customer pays. Transparency builds trust; surprises about missing content create refunds and complaints.

title: Create Your Course in LeadProspectrr
moduleName: Create and Sell Your First Training Programme
learningGoal: Create a course shell, add three lessons, upload content, and preview from the learner's perspective.

items.title: Menu Path
items.description: Memberships → Courses → Products → Create Product → Start from Scratch

items.title: Course Title
items.description: Use a result-focused name. What will the learner be able to do?

items.title: Description
items.description: Clear, result-focused description that tells potential buyers exactly what they will achieve.

items.title: Thumbnail
items.description: Optional but recommended. A simple, clear image that represents the outcome.

items.title: Course Editor
items.description: Open the course editor and add your three lessons using the course-map controls.

items.title: Lesson 1 Content
items.description: Put your prepared Lesson 1 content into its lesson. Attach the worksheet or checklist.

items.title: Save and Publish
items.description: Save and publish content where appropriate. Preview from the learner's perspective before going live.

items.title: Cannot See Courses
items.description: Verify account/sub-account and user permissions. Courses may not be enabled on all accounts.

items.title: File Upload Fails
items.description: Check file size and supported format. Large videos may need compression.

items.title: Course vs Payment Product
items.description: Do not confuse the learning course product with a payment product in the Payments menu. They are separate systems.

keyPoint: The course shell is the container; the lessons are the content. Create a clear title and description, add three action-oriented lessons, upload your prepared content, and always preview from the learner's perspective before publishing. A course that looks good to you but confusing to learners will not sell.

actionSteps.title: Create the Shell
actionSteps.description: Navigate to Memberships → Courses → Products and create a new course with result-focused title and description.

actionSteps.title: Add Three Lessons
actionSteps.description: Use the course editor to add your three action-oriented lessons.

actionSteps.title: Upload Content
actionSteps.description: Put Lesson 1 content and worksheet into the first lesson. Save and publish.

actionSteps.title: Preview
actionSteps.description: Preview the course from the learner's perspective. Check navigation, content display, and mobile experience.

nextLessonTitle: Package a Clear Offer and Price

quizzes.question: Where do you create a course in LeadProspectrr?

options.option_text: Memberships → Courses → Products
Automation → Workflows
Sites → Funnels
Payments → Products

quizzes.explanation: Courses are created in Memberships → Courses → Products. This is the learning content system, separate from payment products or marketing funnels.

quizzes.question: What should the course title focus on?

options.option_text: The result the learner will achieve
The price and discount available
The number of lessons and hours of content
The instructor's name and credentials

quizzes.explanation: The course title should focus on the result. People buy outcomes, not information. Set Up Your First Referral Follow-Up beats Marketing Mastery every time.

quizzes.question: What should you do before publishing the course?

options.option_text: Preview from the learner's perspective
Set the highest possible price
Create marketing materials first
Add as many lessons as possible

quizzes.explanation: Always preview from the learner's perspective before publishing. Check navigation, content display, and mobile experience. A course that looks good to you but confuses learners will not sell.

title: Package a Clear Offer and Price
moduleName: Create and Sell Your First Training Programme
learningGoal: Explain what a buyer gets and create a saleable course offer with clear pricing.

items.title: Result-Focused Name
items.description: The offer name should match the course title and promise a clear outcome.

items.title: Who It Is For
items.description: Clearly state the audience and the problem this solves.

items.title: What Is Included
items.description: Three lessons and the practical tool. Be specific about deliverables.

items.title: Delivery Information
items.description: How they access it, when content is available, and what format it is in.

items.title: Price and Terms
items.description: One price and honest terms including refunds and taxes where applicable.

items.title: Menu Path
items.description: Memberships → Courses → Offers → Create Offer

items.title: Name and Select
items.description: Name the offer and select the correct course.

items.title: Configure Pricing
items.description: Set up free, one-time, or recurring pricing options.

items.title: Publish
items.description: Change from Draft to Published and copy the offer link.

items.title: Review
items.description: Review in a private browser window before sharing publicly.

items.title: Example Prices
items.description: $27, $47, or $97 are examples for a small course, not assumed market prices.

items.title: Value Test
items.description: Ask whether the outcome is valuable enough and whether people in your audience will pay.

items.title: Choose One Route
items.description: Do not mix offer, payment-product, and direct course checkout paths. Choose one working route.

keyPoint: An offer is a promise with a price. It must clearly state who it is for, what problem it solves, what is included, how it is delivered, and what it costs. Choose one checkout route — Offers, Payment Product, or Direct Pricing — and make sure it works end-to-end before sharing.

actionSteps.title: Create the Offer
actionSteps.description: Navigate to Memberships → Courses → Offers and create a new offer for your course.

actionSteps.title: Set Pricing
actionSteps.description: Configure one-time pricing. Choose a price that reflects the value of the outcome.

actionSteps.title: Publish and Test
actionSteps.description: Change status to Published, copy the offer link, and review in a private browser window.

quizzes.question: What is the difference between a course and an offer?

options.option_text: The course is free; the offer is paid
They are the same thing with different names
The course is the lesson content; the offer packages it for purchase or access
The offer contains more lessons than the course

quizzes.explanation: The course is the lesson content and classroom. The offer packages it for purchase or access. One course can have multiple offers (free, paid, subscription).

quizzes.question: What status must a membership offer have before you share it for sale?

options.option_text: Draft
Pending Review
Archived
Published

quizzes.explanation: The offer must be Published before sharing it for sale. Draft offers are not accessible to buyers. Always verify the status before sharing links.

quizzes.question: What should you do when choosing a checkout route?

options.option_text: Let the customer choose their preferred route
Set up all three routes for maximum flexibility
Always use the most complex route available
Choose one working route and avoid mixing paths

quizzes.explanation: Choose one working checkout route: Offers, Payment Product, or Direct Pricing. Mixing paths can create duplicate enrollments and confusion. Test one route thoroughly.

title: Verify Payments and Student Access
moduleName: Create and Sell Your First Training Programme
learningGoal: Understand the complete buyer journey from payment to Lesson 1 and verify every step works.

items.title: Visit Link
items.description: Buyer clicks your offer link and reviews the course and price.

items.title: Pay
items.description: Buyer completes payment through the connected provider.

items.title: Receive Access
items.description: Buyer receives course access automatically or through a grant workflow.

items.title: Sign In
items.description: Buyer signs in to the learner portal or account.

items.title: Open Lesson 1
items.description: Buyer opens Lesson 1 and begins learning.

items.title: Payment Provider
items.description: Confirm a supported payment provider is connected under the account's payment integrations.

items.title: Checkout Display
items.description: Check that the offer/checkout shows the right price, currency, taxes, and course name.

items.title: Published Connection
items.description: Confirm the checkout is connected to the published offer or course.

items.title: Test Purchase
items.description: Run the provider's approved test flow with an email you can check. Never test-charge a real card without consent.

items.title: Access Verification
items.description: In the test learner account, confirm the intended course appears and Lesson 1 works.

items.title: Form Is Not Payment
items.description: A form submission alone is not proof of payment. Do not grant access based on form submission unless payment is verified separately.

items.title: Automatic Access
items.description: Properly connected course-offer purchases can grant access automatically. Do not create a second grant workflow unless genuinely required.

items.title: Record Results
items.description: Record what happened and repair broken steps before sharing publicly. Document any issues and fixes.

keyPoint: A course that cannot be bought and accessed is not a business. Verify every step: payment provider connected, checkout displays correctly, test purchase succeeds, access is granted, and Lesson 1 opens. Test with a fresh email, not your admin account. Document and fix issues before inviting real buyers.

actionSteps.title: Verify Payment Provider
actionSteps.description: Confirm a supported payment provider is connected and configured correctly.

actionSteps.title: Run Test Purchase
actionSteps.description: Use the provider's approved test process. Complete payment with a test email you can check.

actionSteps.title: Check Access
actionSteps.description: Sign in as the test learner. Confirm the course appears and Lesson 1 opens correctly.

actionSteps.title: Document and Fix
actionSteps.description: Record any issues found and repair them before sharing the offer publicly.

nextLessonTitle: Welcome the Customer and Guide Lesson 1

quizzes.question: What should you check immediately after an approved test purchase?

options.option_text: Your bank account balance
That the correct learner has access to the correct course and can open Lesson 1
Social media engagement on the offer post
The number of website visitors

quizzes.explanation: After a test purchase, verify that the correct learner account has access to the correct course and can open Lesson 1. This confirms the entire buyer journey works end-to-end.

quizzes.question: Why should you not grant paid course access based on a form submission alone?

options.option_text: Forms cannot capture email addresses
A form submission does not confirm successful payment
Payment providers reject form-based access
Forms are too slow to process

quizzes.explanation: A form submission alone is not proof of payment. Someone could submit the form without paying. Only grant access after verified successful payment, using Course Grant Offer if needed.

quizzes.question: When should you create a second grant workflow?

options.option_text: For every course to be safe
Only if a separate external checkout or sales route genuinely requires one
For all paid courses automatically
When the first workflow fails

quizzes.explanation: Do not create a second grant workflow unless genuinely required. Properly connected course-offer purchases grant access automatically. Extra workflows create complexity and potential conflicts.

title: Welcome the Customer and Guide Lesson 1
moduleName: Create and Sell Your First Training Programme
learningGoal: Write and automate a welcome message that tells learners exactly what to do next.

sections.title: What a Welcome Message Must Answer

items.title: What Did I Buy?
items.description: Remind them of the course name and the main result they are working toward.

items.title: How Do I Sign In?
items.description: Provide verified login steps or a direct access link. Do not invent a generic portal URL.

items.title: Where Do I Start?
items.description: Point directly to Lesson 1. Remove all friction between welcome and action.

items.title: Where Is the Worksheet?
items.description: Tell them where to find the downloadable resource and how to use it.

items.title: Who Do I Contact?
items.description: Provide a clear support method for questions or technical issues.

items.title: Menu Path
items.description: Automation → Workflows → Create Workflow

items.title: Trigger
items.description: Product Access Granted with the correct product filter. This fires when the learner gets course access.

items.title: Send Email
items.description: Add Send Email action with the welcome message. Optionally add a CRM tag or internal alert.

items.title: Test
items.description: Publish/activate the workflow and test with a fresh student record. Verify the email arrives and links work.

items.title: Existing Notifications
items.description: For some enrollment methods, standard account or portal notifications may already go out. Test actual behavior before adding an extra login email.

items.title: No Resend
items.description: Check messages do not resend unnecessarily when a person already has access. Use conditions to prevent duplicate welcomes.

items.title: Verified Links Only
items.description: Use verified links or the confirmed learner-login procedure. Do not guess or invent URLs.

keyPoint: A welcome message is a map, not just a greeting. It must tell the learner exactly what they bought, how to access it, where to start, where the resources are, and who to contact for help. A confused learner who does not know where to start is a learner who will refund.

actionSteps.title: Draft the Welcome Email
actionSteps.description: Write a welcome message that answers all five questions: what, how, where, resources, and help.

actionSteps.title: Create the Workflow
actionSteps.description: Build a workflow with Product Access Granted trigger and Send Email action.

actionSteps.title: Test Thoroughly
actionSteps.description: Test with a fresh student record. Verify the email arrives, links work, and no duplicates send.

nextLessonTitle: Invite Your First Buyers and Improve from Feedback

quizzes.question: What five things should a welcome email tell the student?

options.option_text: Module outline, lesson count, video duration, certificate details, community link
Instructor bio, company history, testimonials, refund policy, terms of service
Price, discount, expiry, bonus, guarantee
Course purchased, login steps, where to start, worksheet location, support contact

quizzes.explanation: A welcome email should answer: What did I buy? How do I sign in? Where do I start? Where is the worksheet? Who do I contact for help? These five items remove friction and get learners started immediately.

quizzes.question: What trigger should start the welcome workflow?

options.option_text: Form Submitted
Product Access Granted with the correct product filter
Contact Created
Appointment Booked

quizzes.explanation: Use Product Access Granted with the correct product filter. This fires when the learner actually gets course access, not when they register, submit a form, or create an account.

quizzes.question: Why should you test actual behavior before adding a welcome email?

options.option_text: Welcome emails always conflict with payment confirmations
Welcome emails are optional and rarely needed
Testing is only required for paid courses
Some enrollment methods already send standard notifications

quizzes.explanation: Some enrollment methods send standard account or portal notifications automatically. Test actual behavior to avoid duplicate emails and ensure your welcome adds value rather than noise.

title: Invite Your First Buyers and Improve from Feedback
moduleName: Create and Sell Your First Training Programme
learningGoal: Create a small, ethical launch plan and establish a feedback loop for continuous improvement.

items.title: Day 1: Promise
items.description: Finish the promise and course description. Make sure the outcome is crystal clear.

items.title: Day 2: Outlines
items.description: Finish your three lesson outlines and the first lesson.

items.title: Day 3: Upload
items.description: Upload the first version and worksheet to the course.

items.title: Day 4: Payment
items.description: Configure and test payment and access end-to-end.

items.title: Day 5: Welcome
items.description: Test welcome email and learner journey with a fresh test contact.

items.title: Day 6: Invite
items.description: Invite a small relevant group with a clear description and honest availability.

items.title: Day 7: Improve
items.description: Collect questions, identify the next improvement, and update the material.

items.title: The Ask
items.description: Do you want to [desired outcome]?

items.title: The Offer
items.description: I have put together a short training programme that helps [audience] [result].

items.title: The Details
items.description: It includes three lessons and a practical [tool]. Here is what is covered: [brief detail].

items.title: The Price
items.description: It costs [price].

items.title: The Link
items.description: You can see the details here: [tested checkout link].

items.title: Interest
items.description: How many people clicked or asked questions about the offer?

items.title: Conversion
items.description: How many invites led to purchases?

items.title: Completion
items.description: How many buyers opened Lesson 1 and completed the course?

items.title: Feedback
items.description: What questions, refund requests, or support issues arose?

items.title: No Income Guarantee
items.description: Measuring these indicators is more useful than guessing. Data tells you what to improve.

keyPoint: A course that sits unpublished is not a business. Create a 7-day launch plan, invite a small relevant group, and measure real indicators: interest, conversion, completion, and feedback. No income is guaranteed, but data tells you exactly what to improve. A course that evolves based on learner feedback will outperform a perfect course that never launches.

actionSteps.title: Create Your 7-Day Plan
actionSteps.description: Map out each day from promise to first invitation. Set realistic deadlines.

actionSteps.title: Draft Your Invitation
actionSteps.description: Write a simple, honest invitation using the template. No hype, no guarantees.

actionSteps.title: Identify Your First Group
actionSteps.description: Choose 5-10 relevant people who have the problem your course solves.

actionSteps.title: Set Up Feedback Collection
actionSteps.description: Plan how you will collect questions, track completion, and identify improvements.

quizzes.question: What is the purpose of the 7-day first-sale plan?

options.option_text: To guarantee a specific income target
To compete with established course platforms
To create a structured launch and feedback process
To avoid testing the course before selling

quizzes.explanation: The 7-day plan creates structure for launching and gathering feedback. It is not an income guarantee. The goal is to get real learners, measure results, and improve based on data.

quizzes.question: What are two useful early indicators besides revenue?

options.option_text: Course length and production quality
Number of video views and email subscribers
Checkout conversion and Lesson 1 completion rate
Website traffic and social media followers

quizzes.explanation: Useful early indicators include checkout conversion, course sign-in rate, Lesson 1 completion, student questions, refunds, and learner feedback. These tell you whether the course works, not just whether it sells.

quizzes.question: What should your first invitation include?

options.option_text: A detailed comparison with competitor courses
A clear description of the outcome, audience, contents, price, and tested link
Guaranteed results and income projections
Urgency tactics and limited-time pressure

quizzes.explanation: Your first invitation should be honest and clear: the outcome, who it is for, what is included, the price, and a tested checkout link. No hype, no guarantees, no pressure. Ethical marketing builds long-term trust.
